module.purpose: Provides a centralized rate limiting abstraction for the application using the Unkey Ratelimit service. It defines multiple rate limiting profiles (core, common, api, ai, sms, smsMonth, forcedSlowMode) and exposes a rateLimiter() factory that returns a rateLimit function. When UNKEY_ROOT_KEY is missing, or the limiter times out or errors, it fails open with a permissive response so requests are not blocked.
module.summary: This module wraps the @unkey/ratelimit library into a factory function rateLimiter() that constructs a set of named limiter instances, each with its own namespace, request limit, and duration window (e.g. core: 10/60s, api: 30/60s, ai: 20/day, sms: 50/5m, smsMonth: 250/30d, forcedSlowMode: 1/30s). Each limiter is configured with a 5s timeout and an onError handler that logs the failure and fails open (returns a success response) so that Unkey outages do not take down the app. The exported RateLimitHelper type describes the arguments accepted by the returned rateLimit function, including an optional rateLimitingType, a required identifier, optional LimitOptions, and an optional onRateLimiterResponse callback used to surface response headers even when the limit is reached or an error is thrown. If the UNKEY_ROOT_KEY environment variable is absent, rateLimiter() logs a warning and returns a stub function that always allows requests. Inside rateLimit, if the identifier matches an IP ban list, the request is routed to the restrictive forcedSlowMode limiter regardless of the requested type; otherwise the selected limiter enforces the limit. The module also re-exports RatelimitResponse and exports the API_KEY_RATE_LIMIT constant (30).
module.businessContext: This file protects the product's APIs and messaging features (AI, SMS) from abuse and runaway cost by enforcing per-identifier request quotas. If it fails, attackers could spam endpoints or inflate SMS/AI spend; its fail-open design trades strictness for availability.

moduleContractTests.scenario: When UNKEY_ROOT_KEY is absent, rate limiting is disabled and every request succeeds.
moduleContractTests.then: resolves { success: true, limit: 10, remaining: 999, reset: 0 }
moduleContractTests.rationale: Failure-open behaviour is a deliberate availability contract.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An identifier present in the IP ban list is throttled via the forcedSlowMode limiter.
moduleContractTests.rationale: Ban list must map to strictest limiter regardless of requested type.

moduleContractTests.scenario: Omitting rateLimitingType uses the core namespace limiter.
moduleContractTests.then: the core Ratelimit (limit 10 / 60s) handles the call

moduleContractTests.scenario: Each rateLimitingType maps to its configured namespace/limit/duration.
moduleContractTests.when: rateLimit({ rateLimitingType: t, identifier: "x" }) for each of core/common/forcedSlowMode/api/ai/sms/smsMonth
moduleContractTests.then: core=10/60s, common=200/60s, forcedSlowMode=1/30s, api=30/60s, ai=20/1d, sms=50/5m, smsMonth=250/30d
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins the exact limit table as the public rate-limit contract.

moduleContractTests.scenario: An error from the underlying limiter is logged and treated as success.
moduleContractTests.then: returns { success: true, limit: 10, remaining: 999, reset: 0 } and logs the error
moduleContractTests.rationale: Error path must not lock users out; fail-open is contractual.

moduleContractTests.scenario: A limiter call exceeding 5000ms falls back to a success response.
